title: Audit stream fragmentation during KMS epoch handshake timeouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Follow-up ticket for the March 1st incident where audit journal sequences were truncated across multiple shards while an automated KMS epoch handshake retried during a cross-region failover. This ticket coordinates fixes across runtime, audit ingestion, and KMS clients to prevent future loss of compliance-grade audit entries and to provide verifiable reconciliation tooling.
incident_summary: At ~2026-03-01T03:12Z several audit shards reported non-monotonic sequence numbers and missing sequence ranges for customer audit streams. Root cause was a timing window where KMS epoch handshake timeouts caused the audit-writer to evict buffered entries and restart journal segments while the KMS rewrap flow retried. This produced fragmentary journal segments that downstream consumers treated as final, resulting in permanent gaps in the compliance trail for affected accounts.
timeline: 2026-03-01 03:10Z - KMS cross-region handshake latency spike observed as region B experienced intermittent control-plane packet loss
2026-03-01 03:12Z - Audit-writer sidecar detected KMS token refresh timeout and aborted pending writes for 23 active streams
2026-03-01 03:13Z - Autoscaler triggered pod churn in audit-writer pool due to spike in CPU from retry loop
2026-03-01 03:15Z - Monitoring alert: shard sequence mismatch (alerts A-341, A-342); on-call escalated to security and infra
2026-03-01 04:00Z - Temporary mitigation: increase KMS client retry backoff and pause autoscaler for audit-writer deployment
2026-03-01 09:30Z - Initial internal postmortem completed; potential for permanent audit gaps confirmed for a subset of enterprise customers (15 accounts).
root_cause: Race between KMS rewrap/handshake retry and audit-writer journal rotation. On retry failure the audit-writer used a fast-path fail that dropped buffered entries and started a fresh segment without ensuring downstream consumers had a chance to reconcile partial segments. Autoscaler churn amplified the window by evicting in-flight buffers.
immediate_mitigations: Disable aggressive autoscaler upscales for the audit-writer pool during incidents (rolled out 2026-03-01 04:10Z)
Patch KMS client to buffer retry state and avoid signaling 'segment-final' on handshake failures (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit/pull/718)
Backfill attempted for missing ranges using best-effort reconstruction from sidecar crash dumps and in-memory buffers (scripts: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/93321/recon)
Notified affected customers and compliance team; legal & SOC performed initial assessment
long_term_action_items: Implement write-ahead segment commit protocol: audit-writer must persist a segment tombstone only after downstream ack (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 5)
Introduce end-to-end sequence reconciliation in the audit pipeline with automated backfill job that can rehydrate gaps from WAL + S3 + sidecar snapshots (owner: Priya Kapoor, estimate: 8)
Add KMS client circuit-breaker that prevents segment finalization while KMS epoch is unsettled (owner: Riley Patel, estimate: 3)
Improve incident runbook and alerts to classify sequence non-monotonicity as P0 and auto-mute autoscaler for affected deployments during investigation (owner: Operations squad, estimate: 2)
Audit retention & immutable archive test: create a periodic test ensuring that archived segments can be used to fully restore sequences across pods (owner: Security QA, estimate: 3)
Ship an opt-in forensic export for customers to get complete audit artifacts when gaps are detected (owner: Customer Success + Eng, estimate: 5)
Schedule formal security review of the new commit protocol and KMS client changes (security_review_required: true)
